diagnostic_tracker.title: Bigger Smaller Same — Day 1 Diagnostic Checklist
diagnostic_tracker.when_used: During Lesson 1, while children are at the length sorting stations.
diagnostic_tracker.usage_notes: Walk between pairs during the strip-sort and animal line-up. Tick the columns where you see clear evidence; leave blank if not yet observed. The 'Lines up at one end' column is the foundational technique signal — children who don't yet line up can be coached individually before Lesson 2.

formative_trackers.title: Bigger Smaller Same — Lesson 2 Formative Tracker (Mass)
formative_trackers.when_used: During Lesson 2, while children are at the hand-feel and balance stations.
formative_trackers.usage_notes: Stop at each pair. Ask 'Which is heavier? Show me on the balance.' The 'Feels weight by hand' column captures whether the child has internalized the FEEL-FIRST rule from the size-mass conflation walkthrough. Children who only judge by sight need the 'feel, don't guess' re-loop.

formative_trackers.title: Bigger Smaller Same — Lesson 3 Formative Tracker (Capacity)
formative_trackers.when_used: During Lesson 3, while pairs are at the cup-pour and cup-sort stations.
formative_trackers.usage_notes: Stop at each pair. Ask 'Which holds more? Show me by pouring.' The 'Pours carefully' column captures fine-motor practice; the 'Recognizes same capacity' column is the deepest signal — children who only see inequality need the 'same' re-loop.

formative_trackers.title: Bigger Smaller Same — Lesson 4 Formative Tracker (Non-Standard Units)
formative_trackers.when_used: During Lesson 4, while pairs are at the cube/hand-span/footstep stations.
formative_trackers.usage_notes: Stop at each pair. The 'Lines up cubes' column captures the foundational gap-management technique. The 'Picks right unit' column captures attribute-tool reasoning — children who use cubes for everything need the 'right tool for the job' coaching.

summative_rubric.title: Bigger Smaller Same — Summative Rubric
summative_rubric.purpose: Used during and after Lesson 5 (Measurement Carnival Capstone) to score each child against both expectations on a 4-level scale. Aligned with Ontario Kindergarten Communication of Learning conventions.

rows.expectation_text: describe different ways that objects can be measured

levels.descriptor: Cannot yet describe a way to measure. Says 'I don't know' or 'big' without a unit reference.
Names one way to measure (cubes) when prompted. Counts cubes with adult help.
Independently names cubes, hand-spans, and footsteps as ways to measure. Picks an appropriate unit for an object's size.
Names multiple non-standard units AND can describe length using two different units to verify (e.g., '5 cubes OR 1 hand-span').

rows.expectation_text: compare the length, area, mass, and capacity of objects using concrete materials

levels.descriptor: Compares only by sight; struggles with one of the three attributes (length, mass, or capacity). Cannot use a tool (balance, pour) consistently.
Compares length and one other attribute with prompts. Uses the balance or pours with adult support.
Independently compares all three attributes (length, mass, capacity) using appropriate techniques: line up for length, balance for mass, pour for capacity. Recognizes 'same' as a valid result.
Orders 4+ objects across all three attributes AND verifies using a second technique (e.g., compares two cups by both pouring AND counting cubes that fit).

summative_rubric.usage_notes: Score during the Lesson 5 Carnival rotations (mostly visible from the carnival template artifact) and confirm during the consolidation share. Level 3 is the grade-level expectation. Communicate scores to families using the Communication of Learning narrative format.

summative_task_script.title: Measurement Carnival Capstone — Summative Administration Guide
summative_task_script.purpose: Ties the Lesson 5 capstone template, the rotation phases (length / mass / capacity), and the rubric together. Tells the teacher exactly what evidence to look for at each station.
administration_steps: Before the lesson: photocopy one Carnival Capstone template per child plus 5 extras. Print the rubric or maintain a class-wide rubric on a clipboard. Have Junior Measure Captain certificates printed and ready (do not show before earned).

Phase 1 (LENGTH station, 7 min): Children order 4 strips by length, then measure their favourite with cubes. Evidence for A10.1 (cubes) and A10.2 (length comparison). Score the 'Lines up' technique and the cube count accuracy.
Phase 2 (MASS station, 7 min): Children use the balance to find heavier and identify a same-weight pair. Evidence for A10.2 (mass). Score balance use and recognition of 'same'.
Phase 3 (CAPACITY station, 7 min): Children pour to find which cup holds more and identify a same-capacity pair. Evidence for A10.2 (capacity). Score pour technique and recognition of 'same'.

Phase 4 (Share, 5 min): Children share their template with a partner and describe their findings. Listen for unit vocabulary (longer, heavier, holds more, cubes). Use this phase to confirm scores and upgrade Level 4 thinking.
After the lesson: review the rubric with each template. For any child below Level 3, note what evidence drove the decision. Use this for the Communication of Learning narrative.
summative_task_script.scoring_guidance: Use the carnival template as primary evidence and the partner-share as confirming evidence. Level 3 is the grade-level goal. Children who are L4 on both expectations are ready for Grade 1 measurement work. Children L1 on multiple expectations need targeted small-group work — do not retain in K measurement; build the bridge in concrete play.

evidence_per_expectation.A10.1: Look at Part 1 of the carnival template (cube count). Did the child measure their favourite strip with cubes, lining them up tightly? Combined with the partner-share. A child who reports a sensible cube count for a 3in strip (~9 cubes) is at Level 3.
evidence_per_expectation.A10.2: Look at Parts 2 (mass) and 3 (capacity). Did the child correctly label H/L/S on the 3 balance pictures and circle the holds-more cup in 3 pairs? AND did they identify a same pair? A child who scores all 6 questions correctly across mass and capacity is at Level 3 on A10.2.
